name: cppcheck-official
description: A Visual Studio Code extension that runs cppcheck on C/C++ files when they are opened, saved or switched to. Supported by the Cppcheck team.
author: David Ramnerö <david.ramnero@cppchecksolutions.com>

cppcheck-official.enable.markdownDescription: Enable or disable the Cppcheck extension. When disabled, no analysis runs and the warnings of a file are cleared the next time it would have been analysed (when it is opened, saved or switched to).

cppcheck-official.minSeverity.markdownDescription: Minimum severity of the warnings that are shown. This filters what is shown; cppcheck still runs all checks. Can also be changed by clicking **Cppcheck severity** in the status bar. See [Severity filter](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#severity-filter).

cppcheck-official.path.markdownDescription:
Path to the cppcheck executable, e.g. `C:\Program Files\Cppcheck\cppcheck.exe` on Windows or `/usr/bin/cppcheck` on Linux and macOS. If empty, `cppcheck` from the system PATH is used.

Supports `${workspaceFolder}`, `~`, `./` and `../`, e.g. `${workspaceFolder}/tools/cppcheck`. Other relative paths are relative to the workspace folder. See [Paths](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#paths).

cppcheck-official.arguments.markdownDescription:
Additional command line arguments for cppcheck, separated by spaces, e.g. `--project=build/compile_commands.json --suppress=missingInclude`.

The extension always adds `--enable=all --inline-suppr --xml`, and some flags depending on whether a project file is used. See [The command line the extension runs](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#the-command-line-the-extension-runs).

Overridden by `arguments` in `cppcheck.json` in the root of the workspace folder, if present. See [Configuration](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#configuration).

For the available arguments, see the Cppcheck manual ([open source](https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io/manual.pdf#page=4) / [Premium](https://files.cppchecksolutions.com/manual.pdf#page=4)).

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Cppcheck
walkthroughs.description: Learn the basics of using cppcheck in VS Code with the official extension

steps.title: Connect extension to your cppcheck executable
steps.description:
Tell the extension where cppcheck is installed. Skip this step if `cppcheck` is on your system PATH.
[Set path](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22cppcheck-official.path%22%5D)

steps.title: Customize settings
steps.description:
Pass your own command line arguments to cppcheck, e.g. to suppress warnings or enable Cppcheck Premium checks.
[Set up arguments](command:cppcheck-official.configureArguments)

steps.title: Use a project file or cppcheck.json
steps.description:
Point cppcheck at a `.cppcheck` project file or `compile_commands.json`, and share the arguments with your team in `cppcheck.json`.
[Read about project files](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#project-files)

steps.title: Try out the extension
steps.description:
Open a C or C++ file and see the cppcheck warnings in the Problems panel.
[Open the Problems panel](command:workbench.actions.view.problems)

steps.title: Handle warnings
steps.description:
Filter warnings by severity in the status bar, and hide or suppress warnings with code actions.
[Select severity](command:cppcheck-official.selectMinSeverity)

steps.title: Run a full analysis
steps.description:
Analyse every file in your project file at once with the Full Analysis button in the status bar. Needs a project file.
[Read about full analysis](https://github.com/cppchecksolutions/vscode-cppcheck-official#full-analysis)

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
